name: Giannis Antetokounmpo
milestone_by_age_26: Selected 15th overall in the 2013 NBA Draft by the Milwaukee Bucks at age 18, becoming the youngest player in the draft; later named NBA All-Star and Most Improved Player at age 22 in 2017, and NBA MVP at age 25 in 2019.
early_history_summary: Born in Athens to Nigerian immigrant parents, Giannis grew up in poverty in the Sepolia neighborhood, selling goods on the street to help support his family. He started playing basketball around age 12 and signed for Filathlitikos in Greece's second division, averaging 9.5 points and 5.0 rebounds before entering the NBA draft at 18.
family_context_summary: Born to Nigerian immigrant parents in Athens; family lived in poverty and was stateless until 2013. Giannis and his brothers sold goods on the street to help support the family.
primary_early_advantage_tags: poverty, statelessness, physical talent, sibling athletes, NBA pipeline
evidence_summary: Giannis Antetokounmpo was born in Athens to Nigerian immigrant parents who lived in poverty and were stateless until 2013. He began playing basketball around age 12 and progressed through Greece's second division with Filathlitikos before being drafted 15th overall in the 2013 NBA Draft at age 18. His exceptional physical attributes (6'9" with 7'3" wingspan) and athleticism were evident from a young age, but his path was shaped by extreme adversity including poverty, statelessness, and racial discrimination. His brothers Thanasis and Kostas also pursued basketball careers.
starting_point: Born to Nigerian immigrant parents in Athens, Greece; family lived in poverty and was stateless, with Giannis selling goods on the street to help support the family.
current_position: Star forward for the Milwaukee Bucks; two-time NBA MVP (2019, 2020), NBA champion and Finals MVP (2021); estimated earnings ~$93.8M (Forbes); resides in Milwaukee, Wisconsin.

trajectory.event: Selected 15th overall in the NBA Draft by the Milwaukee Bucks and made his NBA debut on October 30, 2013.
Named NBA All-Star for the first time and won the NBA Most Improved Player Award.
Won his first NBA MVP award, averaging 27.7 points, 12.5 rebounds, and 5.9 assists.
Won his second consecutive NBA MVP award and was named Defensive Player of the Year.
Led the Milwaukee Bucks to the NBA championship and was named Finals MVP.
Named to the All-NBA First Team for the sixth consecutive season and became the Bucks' all-time leader in points, rebounds, and assists.

name: Péter Bakonyi
milestone_by_age_26: Won a bronze medal in team sabre at the 1961 Fencing World Championships and gold at the 1961 Summer Universiade at age 23, followed by Hungarian national championship and World Championship team silver in 1962 at age 24.
early_history_summary: Born in Budapest to an intellectual family, Bakonyi began fencing as a youth at the Elektromos Works club and was a youth national team member. He progressed to the prestigious Bp. Honvéd club under coach Somos Béla and broke into the senior national team in the early 1960s, winning his first World Championship medal at 23.
family_context_summary: Born to an intellectual family in Budapest; father was a lawyer and grandfather was an engineer. Due to his class background, he was barred from university admission after graduating from technical school in 1956.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Hungarian fencing ecosystem, elite club, national team pipeline, intellectual family, class barrier
evidence_summary: Péter Bakonyi was born in Budapest to an intellectual family (father a lawyer, grandfather an engineer) but faced class-based discrimination that barred him from university. He began fencing as a youth at the Elektromos Works club and progressed to the prestigious Bp. Honvéd club under coach Somos Béla. By age 23, he had won World Championship bronze and Universiade gold in team sabre, benefiting from Hungary's position as the world's dominant fencing nation and its elite club and national team pipeline.
starting_point: Born in Budapest to an intellectual family; father was a lawyer and grandfather an engineer, but class background barred him from university admission after 1956.
current_position: Retired; former university professor and scientific director at MTA SZTAKI; former president of the Hungarian Fencing Federation (1977-1989); living in Budapest at age 88.

trajectory.event: Won bronze medal in team sabre at the World Fencing Championships and gold at the Summer Universiade.
Won Hungarian national championship in individual sabre and World Championship team silver.

name: Ada Yonath
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Yonath completed her B.Sc. (1962) and M.Sc. (1964) by age 25, but her pioneering ribosome crystallography work began in the late 1970s and her Nobel Prize came in 2009.
early_history_summary: Born in Jerusalem, Yonath completed her B.Sc. in Chemistry at Hebrew University (1962) and M.Sc. in Biochemistry (1964) before beginning her Ph.D. in X-ray crystallography at the Weizmann Institute (1964-1968). Her ribosome structure work, for which she is known, began in the late 1970s.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources in detail. She served in the 'top secret office' of the Medical Forces during compulsory army service before university.
evidence_summary: Ada Yonath completed her undergraduate and master's degrees at Hebrew University by age 25 and began her Ph.D. at the Weizmann Institute. However, her pioneering ribosome crystallography work did not begin until the late 1970s, with the first ribosome crystals created in the early 1980s and the full structure mapped in 2000-2001. She received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2009. No material scientific milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Ei-ichi Negishi
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Negishi received his B.S. from the University of Tokyo in 1958 at age 23 and a Fulbright scholarship in 1960 at age 25, but his foundational Negishi coupling research was published in 1976-78 and his Nobel Prize came in 2010.
early_history_summary: Born in what is now Changchun, China (then Hsinking, capital of Manchukuo), Negishi moved to a town outside Tokyo after WWII where his parents were farmers. He received his B.S. from the University of Tokyo in 1958, worked at Teijin chemical company, then came to the U.S. on a Fulbright scholarship in 1960 to pursue his Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania.
family_context_summary: Born in Japanese-occupied Manchukuo; family moved to a town outside Tokyo after WWII where parents were farmers raising five children.
evidence_summary: Ei-ichi Negishi was born in 1935 in Japanese-occupied Manchukuo and moved to a farming town outside Tokyo after WWII. He earned his B.S. from the University of Tokyo in 1958 and came to the U.S. on a Fulbright scholarship in 1960. His Ph.D. was completed in 1963 at the University of Pennsylvania, and his foundational cross-coupling research (the Negishi coupling) was published in 1976-78. He received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2010. No material scientific milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Franco Bitossi
milestone_by_age_26: Won the mountains classification and four stages at the 1964 Giro d'Italia at age 23, establishing himself as a top professional cyclist after turning pro in 1961 at age 21.
early_history_summary: Born in Camaioni di Carmignano to a humble family, Bitossi began cycling seriously in 1957 at age 17 while working in a factory. He won 13 races as an amateur in 1961 and turned professional that October at 21, immediately winning his first pro race. By 1964, he was winning stages and classifications at the Giro d'Italia.
family_context_summary: Born to a humble family in Camaioni di Carmignano, Italy. His father bought him a used bike, and he worked in a factory while training as an amateur.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Italian cycling ecosystem, humble origins, factory worker, early racing, Tuscany
evidence_summary: Franco Bitossi was born to a humble family in Camaioni di Carmignano, Tuscany, and began cycling seriously at age 17 while working in a factory. His father bought him a used bike, and he trained before and after work. He won 13 races as an amateur in 1961 and turned professional at 21, immediately winning his first pro race. By 23, he had won the mountains classification and four stages at the Giro d'Italia. Italy's position as the heart of professional cycling provided a rich competitive ecosystem.
starting_point: Born to a humble family in Camaioni di Carmignano, Tuscany, Italy; father bought him a used bike and he worked in a factory while training.
current_position: Retired from professional cycling since 1978; living in Empoli, Tuscany, spending time tending olive orchards and lawn bowling.

trajectory.event: Turned professional cyclist in October and won his first professional race.

name: Carlos Pace
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Brazilian national racing championship twice in 1966 at age 21-22, and won the British Formula 3 Forward Trust Championship in 1970 at age 25-26, establishing himself as a top emerging racing driver.
early_history_summary: Born in São Paulo to a wealthy textile merchant family, Pace was encouraged by family friends Wilson and Emerson Fittipaldi to start karting at age 16 in 1960. He moved to cars in 1963, joined the Willys team, and became Brazilian champion twice in 1966 before heading to Europe to compete in British Formula 3.
family_context_summary: Born to a wealthy textile merchant family in São Paulo. His father Angelo Raphael Pace was of Italian descent, and the family lived in Italy for part of Carlos's childhood.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Father was a textiles businessman, not directly in motorsport.
primary_early_advantage_tags: wealthy family, textile merchant, Fittipaldi brothers, São Paulo racing, karting, Willys team
evidence_summary: Carlos Pace was born to a wealthy textile merchant family in São Paulo and was encouraged by family friends Wilson and Emerson Fittipaldi to start karting at age 16. His family's wealth provided the financial platform for his racing career, and the Fittipaldi brothers' mentorship connected him to the Brazilian racing ecosystem. He progressed from karting to cars in 1963, became Brazilian champion twice in 1966, and won the British Formula 3 championship in 1970 before entering Formula One in 1972.
starting_point: Born to a wealthy textile merchant family in São Paulo, Brazil; father was of Italian descent and the family spent part of Carlos's childhood in Italy.
current_position: Died in 1977 at age 32 in a light aircraft accident near São Paulo; final role: Formula One driver for Brabham, winner of the 1975 Brazilian Grand Prix.

name: Antonio Saura
milestone_by_age_26: Held his first solo exhibition at the Libros bookshop in Zaragoza in 1950 at age 19, followed by a solo exhibition at the Museum of Contemporary Art in Madrid in 1956 at age 25, and association with the Surrealist circle in Paris.
early_history_summary: Born in Huesca, Spain, Saura contracted tuberculosis at age 13 and was bedridden for five years, during which he began painting and writing as a self-taught artist. He held his first solo exhibition at 19, traveled to Paris in 1952 and 1954-55 where he joined the Surrealist circle, and by 1956 had begun his major painting series.
family_context_summary: Born in Huesca, Spain. His brother was the film director Carlos Saura. Family background details are not extensively documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Brother Carlos Saura became a renowned film director, suggesting a culturally engaged family.
primary_early_advantage_tags: tuberculosis, self-taught, bedridden, Surrealist circle, Paris avant-garde, Carlos Saura
evidence_summary: Antonio Saura was born in Huesca, Spain, and contracted tuberculosis at age 13, which confined him to bed for five years. During this enforced isolation, he began painting and writing as a self-taught artist, developing a highly personal surrealist style. He held his first solo exhibition at age 19 in 1950, traveled to Paris where he joined the Surrealist circle around Benjamin Péret, and by 1956 had begun his major painting series. His brother Carlos Saura became a renowned film director, suggesting a culturally engaged family. The adversity of his illness paradoxically catalyzed his artistic development.
starting_point: Born in Huesca, Spain; contracted tuberculosis at age 13 and was bedridden for five years, during which he began painting as a self-taught artist. Brother of film director Carlos Saura.
current_position: Died on July 22, 1998 at age 67 in Cuenca, Spain; final role: prominent Spanish painter and founder of the El Paso group.
